svg.text: Which number is the result? Only two bars are the network in Figure 2
Bars are top-5 error, lower is better. Same scale on both sides, so the two competitions can be compared by eye.
ILSVRC-2010 — the clean comparison, all test error
The only year whose test labels are public, so this is where
nearly every experiment in the paper is run.
best entry of the 2010 contest · test
six averaged sparse-coding models · top-1 47.1%
best published since
two classifiers on Fisher vectors · top-1 45.7%
this CNN — the model in Figure 2
one network, ten-patch test averaging · top-1 37.5%
Without the ten-patch averaging these become 39.0% and 18.3%
— the headline already contains a test-time trick.
ILSVRC-2012 — what the winning 15.3% is made of
Test labels not public; the paper finds val and test within 0.1%.
second-best entry of the contest · test
1 CNN — the model this paper describes · val
1 CNN* — sixth conv layer, pre-trained · val
on the 15M-image Fall 2011 release, then fine-tuned
5 CNNs averaged · val (test also 16.4%)
7 CNNs* — the competition entry · test (val 15.4%)
the five above plus two of the pre-trained networks
The abstract quotes both. 37.5% / 17.0% (2010 test) belong to the eight-layer network in Figure 2; 15.3% (2012 test) is an ensemble of seven networks,
two with a sixth conv layer and pre-training on about twelve times more images (15M vs 1.2M). The same single network scores 18.2% on 2012 validation.
